records.text: Alamar Grimm is a warlock trainer who believes arcane magic corrupts only the weak. He resents the gnomes’ dependence on dwarves after the loss of their home and feels dwarven alliances with humans leave gnomes as second-class citizens. He favors special allies who obey without question and teaches the powers needed to command them.

Sten Stoutarm helps newcomers in Coldridge Valley with warm gloves in exchange for wolf meat, calling the bargain an act of kindness. With little help beyond green apprentices who have other concerns, Sten asks visitors for practical assistance, including carrying mail to Talin Keeneye. Sten also passes along a rune thought to come from the warrior trainer Thran Khorman and directs its recipient to Anvilmar.
A young Frostmane troll, speaking in a blunt, threatening voice. It boasts that killing an opponent will be easy and calls for its weapon to drink.
A Rockjaw trogg with a terse, destructive voice. Its few recorded cries reduce its intent to crushing, killing, and destroying.

Balir Frosthammer seeks help driving troggs back from Coldridge Valley, reporting that an attack overran the western camp and left too few hands available. Reports of troggs appearing elsewhere raise concern that the valley’s trouble may reflect a wider threat. Balir hopes the king and Senate are taking steps to address it.

Talin Keeneye hunts the boars around Coldridge Valley, but their recent numbers have made his usual daily hunt dangerous. He also receives mail carried through the pass and forwards a letter addressed to Grelin Whitebeard, showing a practical connection between the two men.
Burly Rockjaw Troggs threaten Coldridge Valley, where Balir Frosthammer seeks help driving them back after trogg attacks. Their cries call for crushing, killing and destruction.
Ironforge Mountaineers offer directions to local services, including the bank and gryphon master.

Grelin Whitebeard investigates Coldridge Valley's Frostmane trolls while his brother Senir examines another part of Dun Morogh. He judges the local threat manageable without the army, though his knowledge of the trolls is limited. Protective of his journal and reports, he is frustrated by his apprentice and seeks more reliable help recovering the stolen journal and delivering his findings.
Grik'nir the Cold uses Frostmane Strength when attacking and casts Frost Shock in combat.
Adlin Pridedrift sells general supplies.

Durnan Furcutter sells cloth and leather armor at Anvilmar. A delivery of scalding mornbrew gives him a welcome break from work: he enjoys the hot drink enough to exclaim over it, then asks the visitor to return the empty mug to Nori Pridedrift.

Branstock Khalder teaches beginning priests in Anvilmar, helping them learn to defend Coldridge Valley against troggs. He encourages further study with Maxan Anvol in Kharanos and invokes the support of the Light and Ironforge. His welcome includes a joke about losing faith in a late arrival, followed by an admission that his jokes are poor.
A Coldridge mountaineer in Dun Morogh.
Donal Osgood is an Arathi Basin battlemaster in Dun Morogh. He politely turns away adventurers who are not yet powerful enough to enter.

Thorgas Grimson is a hunter trainer whose lessons begin with respect for the world a hunter lives in: the beasts that fight beside you, your weapon and ammunition, and the bite of a bitter wind. He treats tracking and surviving in the mountains as traditions that demand courage and cunning, while insisting that most of the work belongs to the student.

Thran Khorman is a warrior trainer in Coldridge who has pledged to help prepare his people to reclaim their home. He speaks matter-of-factly about changes in dwarf life, from dwarves using magic to worship of the Holy Light, and about the trogg threat. He also welcomes the displaced gnomes now living in the city, sympathizing with their flight from a home overrun by Dark Irons.

Solm Hargrin is a Coldridge rogue trainer who keeps mostly to himself, wary that association might give rogues a bad name when things go missing. He values the Ironforge clan’s mutual support and urges dwarves to welcome the displaced gnomes after Gnomeregan’s destruction. He favors a rogue’s blade and shadow over arcane or divine paths, while respecting others’ beliefs.

Bromos Grummner trains paladins in Coldridge and draws on what humans have taught the dwarves about the Holy Light. He respects the tradition of their order and its role in protecting Azeroth, especially the power of individual sacrifice to bring salvation. He sees training as preparation for the work ahead and expects a Knight of the Silver Hand to uphold that role.

Marryk Nurribit is a gnome mage trainer inside Anvilmar. His relaxed, irreverent advice is to avoid trouble, save coin for spells or an ale for him, and stay away from Gnomeregan. He jokes that a few ales impair his hearing and recommends befriending mages for the tricks they know.
Rybrad Coldbank is a weaponsmith in Anvilmar whose services include selling goods and repairs.
A Frostmane novice in Dun Morogh who taunts opponents in rough, blunt phrasing, boasting that killing them will be easy and threatening to turn them into mojo.
Grundel Harkin is an armorer in Anvilmar, offering armor for browsing and repairs. His work provides practical equipment and upkeep for the settlement.
Rockjaw Skullthumpers are aggressive trogg fighters whose blunt combat cries demand destruction, killing and crushing. They attack with head-cracking blows.
A Rockjaw trogg who attacks with a backstab and shouts blunt combat commands: “Destroy!”, “Kill!” and “Crush!”
A Rockjaw trogg who can cast Knockdown and may flee for help when badly hurt. Its threats include “Crush!”, “Kill!” and “Destroy!”
A Rockjaw trogg whose threats include “Crush!”, “Kill!” and “Destroy!” When badly hurt, it becomes enraged and uses Frenzy.
Hammerspine is a rare Rockjaw trogg who bellows “Time to bash!” when attacking and may flee for help when badly hurt.
A Frostmane troll who threatens intruders in a rough, distinctive voice: “My weapon be thirsty!”, “You be dead soon!” and “Killing you be easy.”

A Frostmane troll fighter who threatens attackers with a thirsty weapon and promises to turn them into mojo. In combat, this snowstrider uses Thorns and Faerie Fire; its name may describe a role rather than an individual.

A Frostmane troll fighter whose threats echo the other nearby Frostmane combatants: its weapon is thirsty, killing is easy, and its foe will die soon. This hideskinner attacks with Backstab and flees for help when badly wounded; the name may be a role rather than a personal name.
A Frostmane troll headhunter who taunts opponents with threats of an easy kill and a thirsty weapon, then attacks with thrown weapons.
A Frostmane troll shadowcaster who boasts of Frostmane magic and makes a taunting remark about weed. Its combat magic includes Demon Skin.
Bjarn is a rare beast who can use Ice Claw and Rend Flesh in combat.
Timber is a rare beast who can cast Rabies in combat.
A young wendigo that uses Frost Breath in combat.
A wendigo found in several areas; it uses Frost Breath in combat.
Edan the Howler is a formidable named foe who uses Frost Breath in combat.
Ice Claw Bears are among the wild animals Rejold asks adventurers to cull around Brewnall. They use Ice Claw in combat.
A hostile leper gnome that threatens intruders and uses Decayed Strength in combat.

Maxan Anvol is a priest trainer in Kharanos who guides aspiring priests in the Light. He tests their healing by sending them to tend the wounded Mountaineer Dolf, and sees healing and Fortitude as vital to protecting those who face danger. He offers further priestly training and speaks of growing in strength of body and will.

Magis Sparkmantle is a mage trainer who warns that magic can burn the untrained. He directs promising mages toward a wider calling: taking a place in a secret war, with Jennea Cannon in Stormwind offering a task to begin those lessons. He also passes along a task from his gnome colleague Bink in Ironforge, intended for a mage.

Granis Swiftaxe is a warrior trainer who says the big wars may be over for now, but warriors still need to keep their skills sharp. He directs promising warriors to Muren Stormpike in Ironforge to learn further techniques, and delivers his assessment with a blunt, demanding manner.

Grif Wildheart guides young hunters through choosing a companion. He lends taming rods to try a crag boar, snow leopard, or ice claw bear, comparing their strength, agility, and fighting style. He teaches hunters to tame, call, and dismiss pets, and says a companion can grow in experience alongside its hunter.

Azar Stronghammer trains paladins in the ways of the Light. He offers aid even to those outside the Silver Hand, and points young paladins toward Tiza Battleforge in Ironforge for guidance on the Light and a paladin’s responsibilities.

Hogral Bakkan trains rogues and points aspiring members toward Ironforge’s thieves’ guild contact, Hulfdan Blackbeard. His dialogue limits his training to rogues, and he can provide a letter for the journey.
Kazan Mogosh is a food and drink merchant in Dun Morogh. Customers can browse his goods.
Gamili Frosthide sells cloth and leather armor in the Dun Morogh settlement, serving customers looking for those kinds of gear. Customers can browse her goods.
Boran Ironclink is an armorer in the Dun Morogh settlement. Customers can browse his goods for armor.
Tognus Flintfire teaches blacksmithing. His greeting is warm and informal, and he offers training to those who seek his craft.

Hegnar Rumbleshot is a gunsmith who supplies ammunition to eager buyers near Anvilmar. He relies on Loslor's shipments and can be left short of ammunition when a delivery is delayed. Grateful for fresh supplies, he recalls his grandfather's saying that late is better than never.
Kogan Forgestone is a humanoid in Dun Morogh.

Vosur Brakthel is an apprentice alchemist who learns from Tally in Tinker Town. He praises Tally's expertise and says he learns something new every day, explaining why he works among engineers despite not being one himself.
Innkeeper Belm offers guests a place to rest and supplies to buy. He welcomes visitors to fill a tankard and sit down for stories and shared drink.

Senir Whitebeard is a field investigator in Kharanos, tracking Frostmane trolls and preparing reports for Senator Barin Redstone. He asks for help exploring the troll hold and delivering his report, then requests that his assistance remain unmentioned so others do not think he is neglecting his work. He is also waiting on a report from his brother Grelin and remarks that the cold has put him behind.
Father Gavin is identified with the Argent Dawn.
Foreman Stonebrow is furious about troggs wrecking his quarry work site. He says the stress is harming his health and his aim is no good anymore, so he asks the player to kill troggs for pay.
Prospector Gehn is identified with the Explorers' League.
Quarrymaster Thesten is identified with the Miners' League.
Great Father Arctikus is a powerful, hostile presence at Frostmane Hold. He warns intruders that they have defiled the hold and threatens them, though he can greet someone as a potential companion.

Veron Amberstill is a ram breeder who deals in mighty ram steeds. He presents the exchange as a privilege for proven allies of Ironforge, and says he will show his varieties of rams to those recognized as exalted with the dwarves.
Yarlyn Amberstill is intent on catching Fluffy for a bath. She tries calling the fleeing animal back, offers a year of carrots, and threatens to get her pappy, who catches bunnies with his rifle.

Rudra Amberstill fears for the ranch herd after Vagash takes two rams. With much of King Magni’s army away fighting for the Alliance, she asks a brave visitor to slay the beast and bring back a fang; she warns that Vagash is deadly. Her request is driven by the threat to the herd and the ranch’s livelihood.

Tundra MacGrann is a hunter whose winter supply of dried meat has been stolen by Old Icebeard. He asks for help retrieving the stash from its Thorium-locked meat locker, explaining that his injured leg makes the cave trip too risky for him. Recovering the food matters because he fears starving in the cold season.

Ragnar Thunderbrew is a Kharanos tavernkeeper protective of his family's brewing legacy. He takes the theft of the Thunderbrew Lager recipe personally, raging at the Dark Iron dwarves and urging its recovery. He also shares his Beer Basted Boar Ribs recipe, crediting the malt as its secret. His temper over the stolen ale sits alongside the pride he takes in feeding his patrons.

Ozzie Togglevolt works with Razzle on a possible cure for Gnomeregan's sickness, testing whether irradiated fallout can help. He asks for samples from the irradiated troggs, then seeks stronger, purer fallout from the city's irradiated creatures. Ozzie was beside Gnoarn when radiation caused his hair to fall out, and recalls the injury with theatrical horror. His cure remains experimental: he hopes it may heal a captured leper gnome and restore his own hair.

Razzle Sprysprocket works with Ozzie on the Recombobulator, hoping to reverse the leper-gnome condition caused by the Gnomeregan disaster. He seeks cogs and gears that fit Ozzie's schematics and eagerly makes mechanical adjustments. Confident that the device can save the gnomish race, he is also prepared to return to the drawing board when an attempt goes wrong.

Old Icebeard is accused by Tundra MacGrann of stealing a locked meat chest and taking it to his cave. MacGrann fears losing the provisions he saved for the cold season. Old Icebeard uses Icy Grasp and Daunting Growl in combat.
Grawn Thromwyn is a weaponsmith who sells goods and repairs equipment.

Senator Barin Redstone is impatient with petitioners and quick to threaten dismissal by his guards. Reacting to Senir's report, he angrily questions Magni's authority and Whitebeard's independent action, warning that the Senate will be displeased.
Fluffy is a critter in Dun Morogh.
Apprentice Soren is an apprentice in Dun Morogh.
Cook Ghilm is identified as a Cooking Trainer in Loch Modan, where he offers training.

Prospector Stormpike is an impatient dwarf concerned about a blastpowder shipment he sent to Ironband weeks earlier. He calls encryption a specialty and claims no other scholar can translate a scroll he has been given.
Miner Grothor is a miner.
Miner Grumnal is a miner.

Goli Krumn objects to the goblins' presents and treats, which he believes distract from Winter Veil's meaning. He sees the feast as a time of renewal tied to the winter land and Greatfather Winter, and points curious people to Historian Karnik for its history.

Jarven Thunderbrew is assigned to watch barrels of Thunder Ale at the Thunderbrew Distillery, but the tempting casks test his focus. He admits that a mug would sharpen his wits, then asks a visitor to keep an eye on the barrels while he takes a short drinking break. Once refreshed, he returns to business. During the errand, he sends the visitor to distract him and arranges for the guarded barrel to be replaced by an unguarded one, making the swap possible.

Rejold Barleybrew is a brewer pursuing what he calls the perfect stout. He seeks shimmerweed, a plant used by the nearby Frostmane trolls in their rituals, because its unusual taste might suit an experimental recipe. He also asks for help keeping bears, boars, and snow leopards away from Brewnall Village, so the residents can focus on their work. After developing Shimmer Stout, he wants his brother Wellart, a mountaineer stationed in a border guard tower, to try it.

Marleth Barleybrew is a brewer with a pointed rivalry against the Thunderbrew family: she acknowledges their drinks are good, but insists theirs is not the only decent brew. To make her case, she asks a visitor to sneak a barrel of her Barleybrew Scalder into the Thunderbrew Distillery cellar in place of Thunder Ale, distracting the guard if necessary. She later receives a Thunder Ale barrel as proof of the swap and thanks the visitor, recommending the Barleybrews' stout to anyone who wants a drink with a kick.

Beldin Steelgrill runs a busy mechanic shop and repairs siege engines, including Pilot Stonegear's Trollplow. He works on several engines at once and has little time for new jobs; after running out of a fang-ratchet, he welcomes tools that let him finish repairs.

Pilot Stonegear is a proud, confident driver of Trollplow, a siege engine he is keen to outfit for comfort and greater firepower. He turns Wendigo manes into a proposed cabin rug and seeks volatile incendicite ore for experimental cannon shells. He boasts about surviving a goblin shredder ambush and trusts Trollplow's gun to answer threats.

Pilot Bellowfiz prepares Jetsteam for long Siege Brigade missions, seeking food and bedding while Steelgrill works on his tank. He prizes Rejold Barleybrew's Evershine for warmth and says it can give the furnace a burst of power in a tight spot. Enthusiastic about steam engines, he boasts that he could outpace Stone on the stretch course and chides him for thinking only about fighting.

Vagash is a dangerous creature near Rudra Amberstill's ram ranch. Rudra blames him for preying on the herd and threatens his life to protect the ranch's livelihood. Vagash uses Glacial Roar in combat.
Frostmane Seers threaten opponents with Frostmane magic and accuse them of wanting their weed. They cast Lightning Bolt in combat.
Gretta Finespindle is an apprentice leatherworker frustrated by the time hides take to become usable leather. She looks for a way to shorten the wait and jokes that it cannot be good for her health.

Gryth Thurden is a gryphon master in Ironforge who arranges gryphon travel for travelers. He explains that flights are limited to destinations a traveler has already visited, and offers a route to Thelsamar for those who have been there. Gryth questions whether the Aerie Peak gryphons can withstand the heat of the Great Forge, despite the speed of the Wildhammer steeds. When attacked, he calls for guards.
Avarus Kharag is a humanoid who can cast Hammer of Justice in combat.
The Scarred Crag Boar is a wild boar found across several areas of Dun Morogh and nearby regions. It charges with a rushing attack when it engages a foe.
Thrawn Boltar is a blacksmithing supplies merchant in Kharanos. Travelers can browse his goods, and he also provides repair service.
Kreg Bilmn sells general supplies and ammunition in Kharanos.
Golorn Frostbeard is a tradesman in the Ironforge area who sells goods to travelers.

Loslor Rudge runs an engineering-supplies shop at Steelgrill's Depot. He sent a crate of ammunition to Hegnar Rumbleshot, whose shop serves riflemen and mortar teams practicing nearby, but the courier lost the shipment near the Grizzled Den after wendigo drove him off. Loslor is trying to recover the overdue supplies for a customer who may be running low.
Keeg Gibn sells ale and wine. His role is that of a drinks vendor, distinct from the nearby weapons and engineering suppliers; customers can browse his goods.
Frast Dokner is an apprentice weaponsmith who sells goods and offers repairs. His work combines a developing smith's trade with practical service for customers needing equipment maintained.

Gremlock Pilsnor teaches cooking and speaks of it as a lifelong pursuit, saying he shares that passion with the learner. He points aspiring cooks toward Shandrina at Silverwind Refuge for the Expert Cookbook, reflecting his practical knowledge of where to continue their studies.

Paxton Ganter is a fishing trainer. His trainer services include instruction, while the available training menu also identifies broader talent and specialization services associated with the trainer role.
Dank Drizzlecut is a mining trainer who offers instruction in the profession. He presents teaching mining as his work and invites prospective students to learn from him.
Bronk Guzzlegear is an engineering trainer. His brief workshop remark about making a minor adjustment gives him a practical, hands-on touch alongside his trade.
Uthrar Threx is an apprentice tailor who welcomes visitors with a familiar, folksy greeting: “Welcome to me shop. What can I do for ye?”
A Rockjaw Raider is a terse, aggressive attacker whose shouted commands are “Crush!”, “Kill!”, and “Destroy!”
Tharek Blackstone is a quest giver whose work connects travelers with Beldin Steelgrill's tools and Rejold Barleybrew's new brew.
Kelstrum Stonebreaker trains warriors and takes pride in keeping their skills sharp even when the big wars have quieted. He boasts of a demanding regimen and mocks those he considers unworthy.

Mountaineer Barleybrew is stationed in the southern guard tower near the Loch Modan border. He is eager to share his brother's Shimmer Stout with fellow Mountaineers, and delights in its effect, saying it puts a shine in his eyes and lets him see in the dark. He welcomes visitors hoping for excitement, and says his barrel is nearly dry after days without a good fight.

Pilot Hammerfoot is a Siege Engine pilot and friend of Mori Hildelve. He stayed behind to guard their engines while Hildelve searched for ore, and grew worried when his friend failed to return. On hearing of Hildelve’s death, Hammerfoot grieves him and wishes he could have faced Mangeclaw alongside the player; he says the Ironforge Siege Brigade pilots will remember the deed.

Mangeclaw is identified as a huge Ice Claw Bear in the account of Siege Brigade pilot Mori Hildelve’s last days. Hildelve’s journal says the bear mauled him, though he drove it off; Pilot Hammerfoot believes it later returned and killed him. The account makes Mangeclaw the focus of Hildelve’s final wish for revenge.

Mountaineer Thalos warns travelers that troggs infest the tunnel and may ask those without pressing business to remain in Anvilmar until it is safer. He offers advice and directions to people who need to pass through.

Senator Mehr Stonehallow describes himself as a Senate member and Explorers’ League member who has taken responsibility for the trogg threat at Gol’Bolar quarry. After the attack disrupts mining, he seeks help against the troggs; he then hopes to secure the area with Mountaineers, restore infrastructure, and return miners to work.

Pilot Longbeard serves with the Ironforge Siege Brigade. Friends of his, the Brassbolts brothers, asked him for Siege Engine helmets after their rocket-car pilots kept crashing, but his duties keep him from making the trip himself. He asks for help getting the helmets to them.

Thamner Pol is a physician and First Aid trainer. His guidance points aspiring medics toward more advanced instruction from Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen in Theramore and a book associated with Deneb Walker in Stromgarde.
Barnum Stonemantle is a banker in Ironforge, providing access to banking services.
Bailey Stonemantle is a banker in Ironforge, providing access to banking services.
Milstaff Stormeye is a portal trainer. His instruction concerns the mental aptitude required for portal magic and, for mages, learning to conjure a portal back to this place.
Namdo Bizzfizzle sells engineering supplies, serving engineers seeking materials for their craft.

Sara Balloo is grieving for her beloved Sully. After receiving his letter, she reacts with anguish to the news of his fate. In her own account, she prepared a note to King Magni Bronzebeard and asks someone else to carry it because she feels her grief would hinder her appeal.
Durtham Greldon is a humanoid in Dun Morogh.

King Magni Bronzebeard feels the loss of dwarves fighting for the Alliance deeply and commissions a memorial to Sully Balloo. His daughter Moira and brother Muradin are personal concerns. He seeks to drive the Scourge’s necropolises back to Northrend.

Gerrig Bonegrip collects ancient, powerful lore in Ironforge’s Forlorn Cavern, seeking knowledge he says can open doorways and awaken Those Who Sleep. He values mutual aid among his associates but fears unfriendly listeners and hands. He offers a copy of Yagyin’s Digest in exchange for three items of power and seeks the Lorgalis Manuscript to share its knowledge with his brothers and sisters.

Grand Mason Marblesten of Ironforge’s Royal Stonecutters Union takes King Magni Bronzebeard’s commission for Sully Balloo’s memorial seriously. He seeks fine Alterac Granite for an enduring masterpiece, takes pride in his imagination and craftsmanship, and laments war and Lordaeron’s ruined state.
Peria Lamenur is a pet trainer who teaches hunters to pass training on to their pets. Peria addresses visitors as friends and explains a focus on helping hunters and their companions.

Historian Karnik is an Explorer's League scholar who offers information found in books. Hammertoe's death weighs on him: Karnik says he cared deeply about Hammertoe and turns to his spirit for help understanding Shadowforge activity. He sees that threat as dangerous to Ironforge and directs the response toward the Shadowforge in the Badlands, while sending word to Advisor Belgrum.

Advisor Belgrum acts on the king’s authority in Ironforge and takes Historian Karnik’s reports seriously, urging swift action against the Shadowforge in the Badlands. He wants Hammertoe’s death to have meaning through recovery of the Tablet of Will. He treats its life-giving power as a legend requiring study by the king’s mages, and values allies’ service to the dwarven people.

Ransin Donner exchanges convention secret codes for special prizes, including a murloc pet, a murloc costume and a Big Blizzard Bear. His greeting suggests he may recognize visitors from an exclusive gathering, though he admits the busy city makes recognition uncertain.
Burdrak Harglhelm sells leather armor.
Turuk Amberstill is a dwarven weaponsmith who sells weapons.
Brombar Higgleby is known as the Keymaster.

Librarian Mae Paledust belongs to the Explorers' League and seeks out historical knowledge. She asks for the Monastery's Mythology of the Titans so she can study it and preserve it in Ironforge, believing knowledge of the past may help prepare for what lies ahead.

Lomac Gearstrip is an explosives maker in Tinker Town, known for producing Nitromirglyceronium. When Gaxim Rustfizzle seeks his help, Lomac is wary of taking the request on trust and amused by the prospect of someone exploding; he asks for alchemical ingredients before making another batch and warns that the volatile result is dangerous.
Geofram Bouldertoe is a mining trainer in Ironforge, ready to teach the craft to aspiring miners.
Golnir Bouldertoe runs a mining-supplies shop in Ironforge and takes pride in dwarven miners. He also prepares honorary picks for Brock's pupils, chiseling the students' names into each batch.

Bengus Deepforge trains blacksmiths at Ironforge's Great Forge. He offers instruction in both armor and weapon forging, and greets visitors with a wry reminder that they should have come for more than warmth.
Thurgrum Deepforge is a blacksmithing-supplies merchant in Ironforge. His services include selling goods and repairing equipment.

Ultham Ironhorn teaches riding at Amberstill Ranch. His pamphlet advertises riding lessons and mount purchases; his training includes Ram Riding, with stated gold and Ironforge standing requirements for some lessons.

Lyesa Steelbrow is a tabard vendor. Her conversation offers help for lost Blood Knight, Hand, Protector, and Green Trophy Tabards of the Illidari; the recorded actions recreate the Blood Knight and Hand tabards.
Soleil Stonemantle is a banker. Visitors can open their bank through her service.
Fillius Fizzlespinner is a trade supplies vendor. Customers can browse his goods.
Bryllia Ironbrand is a general goods merchant. Customers can browse her wares.
Dolman Steelfury is a weapon merchant and repairer. Customers can browse his goods and use his repair service.
Grenil Steelfury is a weapon merchant. He offers weapons and repair service to those outfitting themselves, with a straightforward role centered on the practical needs of armed customers.
Bromiir Ormsen deals in heavy armor and offers repairs. His work serves customers looking for substantial protection as well as upkeep for their equipment.
Mangorn Flinthammer is a heavy armor merchant who also offers repairs. He helps customers equip themselves with sturdy protection and keep their gear in working order.
Raena Flinthammer sells light armor and offers repairs. Her trade serves customers seeking lighter protective equipment, along with help maintaining their gear.
Myra Tyrngaarde sells bread and calls out that it is fresh, including oven-fresh bread. Her sales calls make food the focus of her trade, offering passersby a ready staple.
Barim Jurgenstaad sells reagents. His trade serves customers seeking the materials used in spellcasting and other magical work.

Innkeeper Firebrew runs a tavern where guests can fill a tankard, hear stories and make it their home. During Hallow's End, he turns a treat into a playful chicken-clucking challenge, rewarding the performance with an Ironforge Mint. He also points interested adventurers toward Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm's research in Darnassus, while admitting he does not know its details.
Gwenna Firebrew is a barmaid at the tavern. She also offers goods for visitors to browse.

Warrior trainer Kelv Sternhammer believes warriors must keep their skills sharp, even when the big wars seem over. He bluntly tests a visitor's claim to warrior status and offers training. His directions send growing warriors onward to seek instruction from Klannoc Macleod at Fray Island, while another offer points them to the Fallen Hero of the Horde in the Blasted Lands to hear of a warrior's honor.
Bilban Tosslespanner trains warriors. His guidance covers warrior abilities and tactics, while his gossip menu also offers options about resetting talents and Dual Talent Specialization.

Daera Brightspear is a hunter trainer. She offers instruction in the hunter's craft, alongside options concerning talent resets and Dual Talent Specialization. Her greeting uses a Scots-inflected dialect; when a character seeks training outside her class, she directs them to a trainer suited to their class.

Olmin Burningbeard trains hunters in hunting tactics and strategy. He also offers options about resetting talents and Dual Talent Specialization. A hunter seeking further instruction about the Hunter's Charm is directed to Ogtinc in Azshara; the quest describes Ogtinc as a furbolg hunter aiding the Cenarion Circle.

Regnus Thundergranite is a hunter trainer. His conversation offers hunter training, talent resets, and information about Dual Talent Specialization. His greeting uses a Scots-inflected dialect, and he directs characters seeking training outside their class to a suitable trainer.

Hegnar Swiftaxe is an axe merchant who also offers instruction in the art of war. His work brings weapon sales and martial training together; the available greeting does not establish when that instruction is offered.

Brenwyn Wintersteel is a blade merchant, identified by a trade focused on blades. Customers can browse her goods through the native merchant options; the evidence offers no further personal history or view of her work.

Kelomir Ironhand deals in maces and staves, giving his weapons trade a distinct focus among local merchants. His recorded role is practical and centered on browsing those goods; the evidence supplies no personal history or broader outlook.

Skolmin Goldfury is a bow merchant whose trade centers on ranged weapons. Native options allow customers to browse goods and ammunition; the evidence gives no further personal history or attitude to describe.

Bretta Goldfury is a gun merchant, with a trade focused on firearms. Customers can browse her goods and ammunition through native options; no further personal history or outlook is established by the available evidence.

Sognar Cliffbeard is a meat vendor, with a food trade distinct from the local weapons merchants. The evidence identifies this practical role but offers no personal history or further view of his character.
Dolkin Craghelm is a mail armor merchant. His local role is to offer mail armor for browsing; the available evidence gives no further personal history or outlook.
Olthran Craghelm is a heavy armor merchant. His local role is to offer heavy armor for browsing; the available evidence gives no further personal history or outlook.

Fimble Finespindle is a leatherworking trainer. He remembers a cousin accidentally vaporizing all the cloth and leather in Gnomeregan, leaving the place drafty for a while; he recalls those days with amused nostalgia. His greeting also invites the visitor to train, though when it appears is conditional.
Bombus Finespindle sells leatherworking supplies. His recorded local role is a supplies vendor; the available evidence gives no further personal history or outlook.
Lissyphus Finespindle is a light armor merchant. Her recorded local role is to offer armor for browsing; the available evidence gives no further personal history or outlook.

Jondor Steelbrow is a guild master who invites visitors he considers leadership material to organize a guild to fight for the Alliance. His greeting shows an explicitly Alliance-focused purpose; it does not establish whether any visitor qualifies or can complete guild creation.
Pithwick is a bag vendor whose stock is available through his goods menu. His title and service mark him as a practical outfitter for travelers and residents needing carrying gear.
Harick Boulderdrum is a wand merchant. His services also include repairs and quest interaction, making him a useful stop for adventurers tending equipment or seeking local work.
Reyna Stonebranch teaches herbalism. She offers instruction through her training service, a practical guide for those learning to identify and gather useful plants.
Gwina Stonebranch sells herbalism supplies, complementing Reyna Stonebranch’s instruction with the materials herbalists need for their craft.
Edris Barleybeard is a barmaid who sells food.

Theodrus Frostbeard trains priests in their class abilities and talent choices. He also directs a Cenarion Circle appeal to seek out Ogtinc in Azshara, framing aid to those in need as more important than the means. His greetings may invoke the Light or Elune.

Braenna Flintcrag trains priests in the priestly ways, helps them unlearn talents, and discusses dual talent specialization. She calls on the Light in greeting. She also asks for aid to the Cenarion Circle, directing someone to find Ogtinc in Azshara; this reflects a concern with helping those in need.
Toldren Deepiron is a priest trainer who teaches the priestly ways, helps priests unlearn talents, and discusses dual talent specialization. His greetings invoke the Light.

Bink is a gnome mage trainer who sees magic as the fabric of the world and values the care, resolve, and knowledge its study requires. During the flight from Gnomeregan, she left her Mage-tastic Gizmonitor in a hut outside the city; with leper gnomes there, she asks for it back before its energy runs out. Recovering it lets her resume her studies. She also sends mages to consult High Sorcerer Andromath and Tabetha for further instruction.

Juli Stormkettle is a gnome mage trainer. She welcomes fellow mages and recommends befriending a mage, hinting at the tricks their craft can teach. Her training menu also lists talent unlearning and dual talent specialization. (e0001, e0002, e0009, e0010, e0006, e0007, e0008)
Nittlebur Sparkfizzle is a mage trainer. His listed services include mage training, talent unlearning and dual talent specialization.

Valgar Highforge is a paladin trainer who offers aid to those seeking the ways of the Light. He greets visitors warmly and notes that even those who do not follow the Light like a Knight of the Silver Hand can ask for help. His menu lists paladin training, talent unlearning and dual talent specialization.

Beldruk Doombrow is a paladin trainer who offers aid to those seeking the ways of the Light. He greets visitors warmly and notes that even those who do not follow the Light like a Knight of the Silver Hand can ask for help. His menu lists paladin training, talent unlearning and dual talent specialization.

Brandur Ironhammer trains paladins in the Light, emphasizing bravery, protection of the weak and steadfast faith. Brandur admits becoming jealous of accomplished students and says Tiza calls this a weakness he has promised to work on. Brandur refers paladins to Duthorian Rall for further study and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker for the charger trial in Stormwind, and offers the Silver Hand’s aid even to those who do not follow its ways.

Nissa Firestone teaches first aid and encourages students to continue their medical training with Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen in Theramore. She admires his work with Alliance Trauma and presents the chance to study under him as a valuable opportunity.
Ginny Longberry is a reagent merchant. Her services include selling goods, and she also has a questgiver service.
Bingus is a weapon merchant who offers goods for sale. He also provides repairs and has a questgiver service.

Jormund Stonebrow is a tailoring trainer in the Darnassus area. His title and training service mark him as a practical instructor; the available evidence establishes no further biography or personal ties.
Poranna Snowbraid supplies tailoring goods and also has a questgiver service. Her title distinguishes her as a source for tailoring supplies, separate from the cloth armor and robe merchants nearby.

Ingrys Stonebrow is a cloth armor merchant who sells goods and offers repairs. Her role centers on practical clothing and equipment needs; the evidence does not establish additional personal history or relationships.

Maeva Snowbraid is a robe merchant who sells goods and offers repairs. Her specialty sets her apart from the nearby cloth armor merchant, while the available evidence gives no further personal history.

Gimble Thistlefuzz teaches enchanting. His trainer title and training service establish his role as an instructor, but the available evidence does not support further claims about his personality or background.
Tilli Thistlefuzz supplies enchanting goods. Her title identifies a practical source of materials for enchanters; the evidence provides no further personal history or relationships.

Daryl Riknussun is a cooking trainer who says he keeps people fed. For cooks who have outgrown his instruction, he directs them to Dirge Quikcleave in Gadgetzan for further instruction; his own training and advice mark him as a practical guide to advancing the craft.

Emrul Riknussun is a cooking supplies vendor, identified by his title and shop service. The available evidence establishes his practical role in supplying cooks, but gives no reliable details about his personality, relationships, or views.

Grimnur Stonebrand is a fishing trainer who jokes that he is a dwarf made of stone and was not designed to fish. He says he has taught all he knows and points aspiring anglers to his old friend Nat Pagle near Theramore for further instruction.

Tansy Puddlefizz is a fishing supplies vendor. Her title and shop service place her in the practical work of equipping anglers; the available evidence does not establish further details about her personality or relationships.

Burbik Gearspanner is a trade supplies vendor. His title and shop service establish his practical role in providing trade goods, while the available evidence gives no reliable detail about his personality, relationships, or views.

Grumnus Steelshaper trains armorsmiths at Ironforge’s Great Forge. He prizes sturdy armor as the foundation of victory and takes apprentices through a trial of ornate mithril work before shaping their remaining skill. He openly needles Ironus, whom he dismisses as a toy maker and whose weaponsmith path he presents as the wrong choice. His dry, forge-side humor carries into his advice and greetings.

Hulfdan Blackbeard is a rogue trainer and a leader of Ironforge’s Hidden Circle. The Circle values valuables, and Hulfdan recruits operatives to quietly take a share of the riches from the King’s quarry. He treats initiation as a test of whether a recruit is shameless enough to belong, then sends agents on covert errands. When the Circle faces arrest, he turns to his old friend Renzik in Stormwind and urges discretion around the guards.
Ormyr Flinteye trains rogues and passes along Lord Jorach Ravenholdt’s request for a meeting at Ravenholdt Manor. Ormyr says the matter is secret and declines to explain further.
Fenthwick trains rogues and handles changes to their talents. A letter can also be obtained through his conversation options, though the supplied evidence does not identify its message.
Tynnus Venomsprout is a merchant known as a Shady Dealer, offering goods to those who browse his stock.
Hjoldir Stoneblade trades in blades, offering weapons to customers browsing the merchant's goods.

Thistleheart trains warlocks and insists that disciplined training keeps arcane power from corrupting the weak. Thistleheart dismisses those judged insufficiently attuned to darkness, and relays Impsy's request for a meeting and a gift of felcloth as a sign of good faith.

Briarthorn trains warlocks, treating resistance to arcane corruption as a measure of their progress. Briarthorn directs promising pupils to Menara Voidrender, praising her skill in making demon-binding orbs while warning that she offers little praise herself.

Alexander Calder is a warlock trainer who warns that weakness invites arcane corruption and urges continued training. Calder sharply rejects those the darkness does not embrace and relays Impsy's request for felcloth from Felwood.

Springspindle Fizzlegear teaches engineering. Confident in his calculations, he predicts the wheel will soon be obsolete. He praises gnome engineering for useful devices and regards goblin engineering as recklessly explosive.
Gearcutter Cogspinner supplies engineering goods.

Tally Berryfizz teaches alchemy and calls Vosur a talented apprentice and good friend. Tally tells listeners not to be fooled by his beady eyes and bushy beard, adding that talking to him gives Tally a crick in the neck.
Soolie Berryfizz is a merchant selling alchemy supplies.

High Explorer Magellas leads the Explorers’ League’s investigation of the platinum discs found at Uldaman. He sees them as evidence that could illuminate the Titans, the Creators named in the discs, and the dwarves’ enchanted creation. The League is still researching their meaning and where the Plates of Uldum lie; Magellas hopes to send the adventurer who helped uncover the clues back into the field once they have a plan.
Yarr Hammerstone is a mining trainer. He offers instruction in mining to those who speak with him.
The Captured Leper Gnome is a captive who responds with a brief, resigned-sounding “Oh, great.”
Fizzlebang Booms is a fireworks vendor who offers goods for sale.
Bruuk Barleybeard is a bartender who serves food and drink to patrons.
Ironforge Guards direct visitors around the city, including toward the auction house and the bank.
Tisa Martine is a humanoid found in Dun Morogh.

Gimrizz Shadowcog is a warlock trainer who warns that the arcane corrupts the weak and urges students to keep up their training. His other response is sharply dismissive toward someone he says the darkness does not embrace, giving his manner a severe, selective edge.

Roetten Stonehammer manages work for Reclaimers Inc., recruiting help for recovery jobs and arranging payment for completed work. He speaks plainly about the business, values timely results, and can be brisk when busy. In a more relaxed moment he describes the sounds of Ironforge and mentions his wife's pie awaiting him at home.

Tormus Deepforge is a dwarven weaponsmith who seeks equipment for Loch Modan's mountaineers and the human defenders of Redridge. Tormus respects the late mentor Sturgy Ironband and wants revenge on the Dark Iron dwarves who killed those at Ironband's compound. The umbral ore linked to that attack remains a source of interest: Tormus wants to discover its properties and forge weapons from it.

Vejrek is a troll described as the toughest foe nearby, with a hut in the foothills south of Frostmane Hold. Warrior aspirants are sent to bring Vejrek's head to Muren Stormpike as proof of their mettle. Vejrek fights in Defensive Stance and uses Sunder Armor.

Muren Stormpike is a dwarven warrior instructor who tests pupils against Vejrek before teaching them. He stresses that strong defense keeps a warrior standing for the sake of allies, and warns never to show one's back to a foe. After instruction, he recommends Tormus Deepforge for a suitable weapon.

Tog Rustsprocket is a gnome resident near Kharanos. Snow bothers him because it soaks his robe and disrupts his work. When asked to judge a mock speech for High Tinker Mekkatorque, he calls it horrible, then allows that it might only need a little cleaning up. This reaction suggests he is willing to soften a blunt first impression.

Lago Blackwrench is an Ironforge warlock who directs novices to Gakin the Darkbinder in Stormwind for training. Lago resents relocation from Gnomeregan and says Magni’s watch forces the warlocks to send students elsewhere, though Gakin is a capable teacher. Lacking the materials to teach felhunter summoning locally, Lago refers students to Strahad Farsan in Ratchet, a fellow member of the inner circle, and offers to send word ahead.

A Dark Iron Spy voices the same brief threats as Captain Beld: warnings against crossing a Dark Iron, a death threat, and a boast about the power of the Dark Iron Dwarves. When badly wounded, it flees for assistance.

Captain Beld is identified as a Dark Iron Captain. His combat lines match those of the Dark Iron Spy: he warns against crossing a Dark Iron, threatens death, and boasts of the Dark Iron Dwarves' power.

Klockmort Spannerspan is an eager craftsman in Ironforge, excited to test Furen Longbeard’s new technique on armor of his own. He gathers unusual materials and mechanical components for his work, then proudly reports that the process made the finished armor remarkably resilient.

John Turner runs a Stormwind orphanage with his wife, Stephanie, and makes regular trips to Ironforge to seek supplies and support. He is especially concerned with getting linen home so his wife can make clothes for the children. Though the trip keeps him from Stephanie and has been slow, he remains grateful to those who help the orphanage.

Narm Faulk and Muiredon Battleforge investigated Dark Iron activity near Helm's Bed, where they saw the captain giving orders. When the dwarves overwhelmed them, Narm held them off so Muiredon could escape, but fell before securing the orders. Rescued with the Symbol of Life, he asks that the recovered script be taken to Muiredon, who can present proof to Ironforge's council.

Muiredon Battleforge is Narm Faulk's close friend and fellow investigator of Dark Iron activity near Helm's Bed. Wounded in their failed attempt to seize the captain's orders, he escaped when Narm stayed behind and fell. After recovering, Muiredon welcomes the script as proof for his wife to take to Ironforge's council, then hopes to return to the investigation despite his wife's concern.

Tiza Battleforge guides Ironforge paladins through tests of charity, patience, and readiness to wield the Light. She asks them to help someone in need, then to aid her wounded husband, Muiredon, with the Symbol of Life. Tiza judges their worthiness and offers another Symbol if they fail to save Muiredon and Narm, while warning that repeated failure may count against them.

Jordan Stilwell is a faithful friend of the paladins, though he chose his father's smithing craft over becoming one himself. He offers to forge a weapon for a paladin who gathers the materials, and recovering his father's hammer and a Kor gem moves him deeply. Jordan also thanks the adventurer who reports that his wife is safe, then begins forging the promised weapon and takes pride in supporting the Light through his craft.

A Caverndeep Invader is one of the humanoids encountered among the Caverndeep. When affected by Radiation, it is associated with the blood-spray outbreak, marking it as one of the invaders caught up in the irradiated threat.
The Caverndeep Looter is an armed humanoid of the Caverndeep group. It fights with a weapon and can cast Grab Weapon in combat; radiation can also leave it irradiated.

A Caverndeep Pillager is one of the humanoids of the Caverndeep group. It is caught up in the radiation outbreak, becoming irradiated when splashed by the blood; its name marks it as a pillager among those invaders.
An Irradiated Invader is a humanoid already marked by the outbreak. In combat it can cast Radiation Bolt, making it an active part of the irradiated danger around the Caverndeep.

The Addled Leper is a deluded defender who mistakes others for trogg invaders and answers them with threats. Their sickness clouds their sight, but their words insist that no gnome be left behind; they see themselves as holding the line against the troggs.

Techbot presents itself as an information and help bot, inviting visitors to whisper for answers. It asks to be treated kindly, jokes uncertainly about a hidden “COW level,” and describes handling people in the order they appear on its screen. Its speech mixes helpful reassurance with computer-like queue announcements.
Balthus Stoneflayer is a skinning trainer.

Krom Stoutarm is an itinerant warlock who spends time in Ironforge's library, collecting ancient texts. He recalls books closely and can point seekers toward catalog references, including for the lost Tome of the Cabal. He also asks for help recovering a treasured possession left in his chest at the Uldaman excavation after troggs drove him out; its return matters to him personally, and he offers honor and coin for its recovery.
Dannie Fizzwizzle is a humanoid in Dun Morogh.
Wren Darkspring is a named individual found in Dun Morogh.

Jubahl Corpseseeker is associated with the warlock dreadsteed quest. Its instructions direct warlocks to Mor'zul Bloodbringer at the Altar of Storms to begin the perilous ritual for binding a dreadsteed.

Gnoarn blames the troggs for Gnomeregan's destruction and for the radiation that cost him his hair. Still furious, he hopes the city can be saved: he asks for help locating the missing reconnaissance agent Bingles Blastenheimer, directs an assault-related appeal to Shoni the Shilent, and points toward Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle's proposed solution.

Hands Springsprocket asks a capable traveler to carry a package to Kharanos after crossing the pass, since he cannot get through it himself. With the pass disrupted by troggs and a Mountaineer escort still days away, he needs the inn supplies delivered to Tannok Frosthammer.

Tannok Frosthammer is the innkeeper's assistant in Kharanos. When Hands's supplies arrive, Tannok says the troggs' takeover of the pass has cut off word from Anvilmar. He thanks the courier and welcomes them to rest by the fire with a flagon of ale.

Talvash del Kissel is an Ironforge jeweler whose reputation and business have suffered after a dispute with a competitor. He trades information about a necklace for materials, explaining that he crafted it for a paladin who died while pursuing a cause in Uldaman. Talvash offers to restore the necklace with a powerful construct's energy and also proposes improving a ring for a fee and materials.

Onin MacHammar is a dwarf informant working near Gnomeregan while concealed among the lepers. He reports the armored quarry shipment's route and refueling stop to the Hidden Circle, whose agent asks him to keep quiet. Onin sends his report to Hulfdan in Ironforge, giving the group information for its plans concerning the quarry shipments.

Dinita Stonemantle administers the Vault of Ironforge and honors valuable reward vouchers from the Explorers' League. The League authorizes Dinita to offer compensation from its vault, including a choice of healing or mana potions.
Demnul Farmountain is a humanoid in Dun Morogh.

Dink is a gnome mage instructor who recommends befriending mages for their hidden tricks. Dink speaks of a secret war and sends promising pupils to Jennea Cannon in Stormwind for the beginning of their true lessons.
Gnomeregan evacuees seek escape, expressing anguish at coming so close to getting away.
Lyon Mountainheart is a named individual found in Dun Morogh.

High Tinker Mekkatorque, King of the Gnomes, is determined to reclaim Gnomeregan for his displaced people. He regards Mekgineer Thermaplugg as a betrayer of his trust and wants him destroyed. His enthusiasm for invention extends to imagining Light-powered devices that could fight the Scourge.

Tinkmaster Overspark is a leading gnomish engineer and trainer in Ironforge, advocating gnome-oriented techniques and the continued prominence of gnomish invention. He created Techbot, once a helpful repository of information, and hopes to recover and repair it after its behavior changed when Gnomeregan fell. He also assesses engineers’ work to guide their craft toward gnomish methods.

Master Mechanic Castpipe organizes high priority missions into Gnomeregan to recover data left behind during the gnomes' flight. His work centers on reaching the city's high security terminals and retrieving a prismatic punch card; he describes the lost information as vital to the gnomes and asks adventurers to help with the dangerous recovery effort.

Binjy Featherwhistle is a mechanostrider pilot at Steelgrill's Depot. He teaches mechanostrider piloting and is also associated with riding instruction advertised to Dun Morogh residents. His training dialogue identifies Gnomeregan Exiles standing as relevant to learning mechanostrider piloting.

Milli Featherwhistle is a mechanostrider merchant at Steelgrill's Depot, where she presents the latest models and sells mounts. When a playback device presents one of Toby Ziegear's proposed speeches for High Tinker Mekkatorque, Milli objects that she does not understand it and calls it terrible, giving a notably blunt response to the draft.
Thalgus Thunderfist is a weapon merchant.
Bimble Longberry sells fruit, including fresh apples, and advertises it as coming from Elwynn's lush forests. Her brief sales lines focus on freshness and ripe fruit.
Wizbang Booms is identified as a holiday fireworks vendor.

Curator Thorius cares deeply about the museum and its collection: Margol the Rager's horn excites him, and he welcomes the chance to display it. He grieves Dorius and vows to carry out his final request by freeing the archaeologist's enslaved men and seeking justice for their murder. The betrayal behind Obsidion also strikes personally: Thorius learns his own brother arranged it, condemns that betrayal of him and Ironforge, and fears Ragnaros and the Old Gods' influence leave no one safe. He offers visitors a museum tour and handles its acquisitions with enthusiasm.
Sprok is associated with the Away Team.

Felix Whindlebolt is a Gnomeregan refugee who fled when radiation made his home uninhabitable. In his escape he lost his personal belongings and tools, which trolls took to camps southwest of Anvilmar. He asks for them back with evident anxiety about the dangers around him, then greets their return with heartfelt gratitude.
Gibblewilt is a formidable gnome who threatens attackers and casts Lightning Bolt in combat.

Tymor is a student of arcane history with a particular interest in Azshara's elven past. He has begun investigating its ancient cities and seeks rubbings of their magical runes for study at his tower. Excited by the discoveries and eager to examine the rubbings, he arranges for pilot Xiggs Fuselighter to carry them safely from the region.
Gretta Ganter sells fishing supplies.

Xiggs Fuselighter is an airship pilot who owes Tymor a favor and agrees to help move his Azshara research by air. He describes a coastal patrol and a small island landing pad as the pickup point, while cautioning that reaching a signal may take time. In Ironforge he is also preparing his ship for a long voyage, seeking wendigo manes to line its cockpit from the tank pilots.
Auctioneer Buckler serves customers through the auction service.
Outfitter Eric specializes in tailoring supplies, which customers can browse.
Auctioneer Redmuse handles customer access to the auction service.

Royal Historian Archesonus guides the study of Dark Iron history. He offers a brief account of the Dark Iron dwarves and directs inquiries to the Ruins of Thaurissan to recover information from relics, warning that guardians protect whatever secrets remain. When findings are brought to him, he treats them as part of a larger history still to learn.

Sraaz sells cherry pies and speaks about them with unmistakable enthusiasm. He praises their taste, calls pie his favorite food, and repeats Nana’s lesson that a warm, homemade slice is one of life’s greatest pleasures.

Laris Geardawdle is a gnome researcher in Ironforge who studies oozes and slimes. He gathers samples to investigate where they come from and how they adapt to their surroundings, and suspects they may be tied to Azeroth’s creation. He hopes his work will earn him recognition among the Explorers’ League and show that admitting gnomes to Ironforge after Gnomeregan was no mistake.
Auctioneer Lympkin handles auction business.
Shelby Stoneflint is a stable master who helps with stabling pets and recovering lost companions.
Ulbrek Firehand is a stable master who handles pet stabling and helps recover lost companions.

Belia Thundergranite trains hunters and their pets. She teaches pet training and can explain untraining; she says she helps hunters and their pets. Her guidance emphasizes respecting and caring for a pet, which she describes as a loyal friend in return.
Rotgath Stonebeard is an apprentice blacksmith from a family of smiths. His father and grandfather worked as smiths, and his son now follows the same trade, a source of pride for Rotgath.
Groum Stonebeard is an apprentice blacksmith. He is occupied finishing an order for his father, who expects him to complete the work.
A humanoid named Binny Springblade in Dun Morogh.
A humanoid named Prynne in Dun Morogh.
Angus is part of a Dwarven Mortar Team, taking part in its coordinated activity.
Shorty is part of a Dwarven Mortar Team. He animates and fires the mortar, distinguishing his role in the team's coordinated activity.

Courier Hammerfall serves as a messenger for news from across the continents and directs interested visitors to established contacts. His notices point toward the Cenarion Circle's frontier call, the fight against the Scourge in the Plaguelands, and a request from Feathermoon Stronghold.

Jemma Quikswitch is an apprentice engineer whose enthusiasm is fixed on the coming Henweigh 6000. She says she can barely contain her excitement at hearing that the machine will soon leave the assembly line, revealing a fascination with engineering's new inventions.

Trixie Quikswitch is an apprentice engineer absorbed in an oversized invention: a twenty-foot turkey baster. She says the plans are nearly complete, and treats finding a turkey of matching size as the remaining obstacle.

Thonys Pillarstone is an apprentice enchanter who hints that steel can be strengthened through means beyond ordinary hammer and forge work. His advice points visitors toward enchantment as a craft that can complement a smith's skill.

Myolor Sunderfury is a blacksmith and keeper of the Great Forge. He directs interested smiths toward Derotain Mudsipper in Gadgetzan to learn how to make imperial plate armor, connecting his forge-side role with a specialist's instruction.

Ironus Coldsteel trains weaponsmiths and asks aspiring smiths to demonstrate their skill by making a set of blades, axes, and maces. When the work is brought back, he says customers are waiting and calls it the first step in a weaponsmith's career.

High Priest Rohan teaches priests and holds that the reason for helping those in need matters more than the method. He provides a censer used in his own exorcisms for Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker's undertaking, preparing it with fresh incense and three blessings. He explains that the donation replaces the censer and helps replenish food for Ironforge's needy.
Tristane Shadowstone guides young hunters toward earning an animal companion, referring them to taming teachers such as Dazalar, Grif Wildheart and Huntress Kella Nightbow.
Buliwyf Stonehand is a weapon master whose brusque welcome urges would-be pupils to speak up rather than stand slack-jawed.
Yori Crackhelm welcomes heroes in Kharanos and exchanges special gift vouchers for companion gifts, greeting recipients warmly and calling them special heroes.
A mountaineer of the Stormpike forces.
Glordrum Steelbeard is an Alterac Valley battlemaster who asks prospective fighters whether they understand the opposition and are ready to face the Frostwolf Clan.
A blue mechanostrider, a mechanical character found in Dun Morogh.
Icy Blue Mechanostrider Mod A is a mechanical character found in Dun Morogh.
A red mechanostrider, a mechanical character found in Dun Morogh.
Unpainted Mechanostrider X is a mechanical character found in Dun Morogh.
A Green Mechanostrider in Dun Morogh.
A White Mechanostrider Mod A in Dun Morogh.
A brown ram.
A gray ram.
A white riding ram.

Mountaineer Dolf is a mountaineer wounded badly enough to need a priest's healing. In his own words, he thanks the priest for arriving in time, says the Light will help him take on the wendigo, and wishes the departing visitor the Light's blessing. His brief exchanges convey gratitude and religious conviction.

Nori Pridedrift is a Coldridge Valley courier whose scalding mornbrew delivery to Durnan Furcutter has been delayed by an earlier stop at Grelin's. She presses a passerby to carry the drink while it is still hot and asks for her mug back. She checks on the delivery and, when the mug is returned, celebrates with a practical joke about mugs not growing on trees, giving her a brisk, good-humored concern for the details.

A mounted Ironforge mountaineer in combat, this unit uses a ranged shot and may flee for assistance when badly hurt. Its field-fighter role and mounted form distinguish it within the mountaineer forces.

This gnome engineer's gossip centers on engineering rivalry at the races: they praise gnomish ingenuity, boast about modifying their car and predicting its performance, and mock the goblins' vehicle and luck. One remark claims their son could design a faster car. The mix of technical pride, confident predictions, and family bragging gives the engineer a competitive, showy voice.
A mountaineer in Dun Morogh.

Bixi Wobblebonk is a weapon master who greets visitors with an informal welcome and asks whether they want to learn proper technique with a new weapon. Her conversation also points to other weapon masters as a source of training.
Wulmort Jinglepocket represents Smokywood Pastures as a warm, exuberant Winter Veil merchant, urging visitors to stock up on treats and festive wrapping paper.

Macey Jinglepocket is a Smokywood Pastures seasonal seller, cheerfully pitching the farm's treats, wrapping paper and holiday bargains. Their sales patter mixes jingling-pocket wordplay with a craving for chestnuts by an open fire, and they direct visitors to tell Greatfather Winter what gift they hope for.

Greatfather Winter presents himself as a genial Feast of Winter Veil figure, greeting visitors with seasonal wishes and joking in the third person even while asking for cookies and milk as a treat. The greetings credit Smokywood Pastures and link holiday treats and hoped-for gifts with good behavior, while holding out treats as a possibility rather than a promise.

Lieutenant Rotimer is identified as a Stormpike Guard Recruitment Officer. His recruitment pitch presents the fight against the Frostwolf Clan in Alterac Valley as an Ironforge territorial imperative, then directs recruits to report to Lieutenant Haggerdin to begin their service.

Artilleryman Sheldonore handles an ammunition exchange. After a shipment from Kharanos leaves him with unwanted arrows, he offers to trade them straight across for thorium shells; his response calls the shipment rubbish and the arrows flimsy, showing his blunt, exasperated manner.
Thief Catcher Shadowdelve is a named combatant who casts Hooked Net in combat.
Thief Catcher Farmountain is a named combatant who casts Hooked Net in combat.
Thief Catcher Thunderbrew is a named combatant who casts Hooked Net in combat.
The Swift Brown Ram is a ram.
A swift white ram.
A swift gray ram.
A Swift Yellow Mechanostrider in Dun Morogh.
A Swift White Mechanostrider in Dun Morogh.
A Swift Green Mechanostrider, a mechanical creature.

Mistina Steelshield serves as Ironforge's Alliance Cloth Quartermaster. In her donation appeal, she says the city's cloth stores are running low and urges visitors to contribute cloth found while adventuring, describing the gifts as a way to earn recognition from Ironforge's dwarves. She frames replenishment as a community effort.

Bubulo Acerbus is the Alliance Cloth Quartermaster associated with the Gnomeregan Exiles' cloth drive. He speaks for the exiles, describing dwindling reserves and asking for donations. His appeals stress the respect cloth gifts earn from the gnomes, and his runecloth appeal thanks a donor for earlier help; his pitch adds a wry aside that cloth can buy respect after all.

Melnan Darkstone is a Darkmoon Faire barker who announces the carnival's arrival in exuberant, theatrical calls. He urges children and adults alike to experience its show and reminds visitors that the Faire stays open only briefly, giving his promotion a lively, time-sensitive edge.

Lylandris is the Warsong Gulch battlemaster. She can apologize to a combatant who is not seasoned enough to enter, or call for help in the fight against the Warsong Outriders. She recruits support for the battleground.

Wagner Hammerstrike is a Harvest Festival participant who invites visitors to remember ancestors and past heroes, share the feast, and celebrate with fireworks. He speaks with deep respect for Uther Lightbringer, recalling the paladin’s anguish at Arthas’s betrayal and his final effort to protect others. Wagner’s tribute asks visitors to honor Uther at his tomb.
An Honored Hero in Dun Morogh.

Barrus is the Fishing Promoter for a Stranglethorn fishing contest. He welcomes skilled anglers and explains the rules for the Sunday event, where a master angler will be chosen; his associated quest offers a fishing flier.

Jademoon is a named Cenarion emissary associated with the call to defend Silithus from the silithid. The call describes Cenarion Circle forces gathering and directs recruits to Windcaller Proudhorn at Cenarion Hold for instructions.
Katrina Shimmerstar is a Hallow's End treats vendor who offers goods for shoppers to browse.

Sergeant Stonebrow is an upbeat Alliance collector in the Ahn'Qiraj war effort, asking for copper bars to make war materiel. He welcomes repeat contributions and says the copper will help build steam tanks and, if time allows, gyrocopters. His thanks are warm, and he accepts that a donor may have bought the bars rather than mined them.

Corporal Carnes is an Alliance iron collector supporting the Ahn'Qiraj war effort's weapons, armor and vehicles. He needles returning donors about his low opinion of them, then admits their efforts make him feel gooey inside. Beneath the dry teasing, he thanks contributors and urges them to keep helping the war effort.

Dame Twinbraid oversees the Alliance’s thorium collection for the war effort, including bars intended for steam tanks bound for Silithus. She speaks warmly of receiving a shipment from her brother and dryly wonders why Gnoarn doubts her reconnaissance abilities.

Private Draxlegauge collects stranglekelp for the Alliance’s Ahn’Qiraj war effort. Draxlegauge talks exuberantly about the herb’s many uses, jokes about being tempted to skim some from the stacks, and is quick to pack each delivery before it withers. Even after another batch arrives, the answer to whether more is needed remains an emphatic yes.

Master Nightsong presents themself as an authority on purple lotus and its applications, overseeing its preservation for the Alliance war effort. The measured appeals for more herbs are practical as well as scholarly: Nightsong says they will support potions and oils for troops, and notes that the Horde is gathering purple lotus too as the silithid threat grows.

Sergeant Major Germaine is a practical Alliance officer organizing Arthas' Tears for the Ahn'Qiraj war effort. He says he is following orders and does not know what the herbs are for, but values volunteers who follow through. His direct manner and praise for dependable help make him an earnest, task-focused organizer.

Bonnie Stoneflayer brings her family's long tradition of skinning to the Alliance war effort, overseeing the proper tanning of donated light leather. She is attentive to making good use of the skins and speaks with warm, encouraging courtesy, inviting helpers to return when more material is needed.

Private Porter has been charged with collecting and tracking medium leather for the Alliance war effort, and speaks in terms of meeting his quota. He is earnest about putting every donation to use and openly grateful for help; his relaxed, folksy turns of phrase give his requests an approachable tone.

Marta Finespindle is an upbeat, practical organizer for the Alliance's Ahn'Qiraj leather drive. She says she has been put in charge of tracking thick leather and imagines it made into armor, weapons, steam-tank fittings, rifle scopes and engineering goggles. Her enthusiasm comes through in her eager appeals for more and her playful suggestion that any surplus could even go to the Horde for zeppelins.

Sentinel Silversky speaks formally and solemnly about the coming Ahn'Qiraj war, describing it as long and bloody. Asked to lead the linen-bandage collection, she sees it as practical preparation for the Alliance's forces. Her praise emphasizes selflessness and service to both the Alliance and Azeroth; she invokes Elune's blessing and says she will make the Alliance aware of contributors' efforts.

Nurse Stonefield has been placed in charge of collecting silk bandages for the Alliance as the Ahn'Qiraj War looms. She frames the work as making sure soldiers have the supplies they need. Her replies warmly thank contributors and describe their help as selfless; she hopes their aid will help determine whether the war effort succeeds.

Keeper Moonshade is a formal, earnest supporter of the Alliance’s war effort. They collect runecloth bandages so soldiers and the people around them have a better chance of surviving the coming conflict. Moonshade thanks contributors warmly and urges them to return with more supplies.

Slicky Gastronome is a gnome with an exuberant, teasing manner and an obvious appetite. He presses for cooked rainbow fin albacore to feed Alliance soldiers, jokes with returning helpers, and sings of setting aside a share for himself. He readily invites people to bring him another batch.

Sarah Sadwhistle is a reluctant volunteer in the effort to gather food for the war at Ahn’Qiraj. She says her father thought the work would be a good learning experience, though she dislikes meat. Her dry, weary thanks and complaints about the roast raptor show little enthusiasm for the task.

Huntress Swiftriver coordinates Alliance provisions for the coming Ahn’Qiraj campaign, stockpiling spotted yellowtail for soldiers. Practical and appreciative, she treats food preparation as part of the war effort and invites experienced helpers to bring another catch.

General Zog bears the title Horde Ambassador. The Horde’s Ahn’Qiraj war-effort notice directs contributors to bring singed corestones to him in Durotar, placing him as a named collection point in that campaign.

Elder Goldwell is honored as an elder in the seasonal quest “Goldwell the Elder.” A seasonal greeting links the new year and bright moon with the awakening of the ancients; gossip options let visitors ask about Elders Bronzebeard, Ironband and Silvervein.
A War Effort Volunteer, a humanoid in Dun Morogh.

Field Marshal Snowfall commands a war effort and authorizes exchanges of signets for supplies. Snowfall encourages contributors, stressing that enough materiel and everyone doing their part are essential to victory.

Master Sergeant Fizzlebolt recruits aid for the Alliance's preparations for the Ahn'Qiraj War. Fizzlebolt says the collectors cannot meet their material goals without volunteers and directs helpers to Field Marshal Snowfall in Ironforge's Military Ward.
A Darnassus commendation officer who exchanges signets and recognizes the sacrifices made to earn them, praising adventurers for their service.

A Smokywood Pastures operator responsible for the PX-238 Winter Wondervolt. The operator encourages visitors to try it but asks them to sign forms because bugs remain, and regrets being unable to visit Winter's presents while tending the machine. Visitors are encouraged to seek those gifts in Ironforge or Orgrimmar.
Gnomeregan's Commendation Officer handles commendation signets and recognizes adventurers' service. The officer offers further help when adventurers have more signets to hand in.
Ironforge's Commendation Officer handles commendation signets and recognizes adventurers' service. The officer offers further help when adventurers have more signets to hand in.
Stormwind's Commendation Officer handles commendation signets and recognizes adventurers' service. The officer offers further help when adventurers have more signets to hand in.
A helper associated with Greatfather Winter, this figure announces that Father Winter has left presents beneath the tree for everyone.

Officer Porterhouse represents the Gnomeregan Exiles as a Commendation Officer. Porterhouse accepts Alliance Commendation Signets in different quantities and says handing in ten at once is most beneficial. The officer records adventurers' deeds, earning recognition for their service, and offers further help with more signets.

Officer Ironbeard is Ironforge’s Commendation Officer, recording adventurers’ deeds when they exchange Alliance Commendation Signets. He accepts signets in different quantities and recommends handing in ten together for the most beneficial exchange. He regards the signets as recognition of service to Ironforge and welcomes further exchanges.

Elder Bronzebeard speaks of the Lunar Festival as a time of renewal: the year is new, the moon shines bright, and the ancients awake. Visitors also ask him where to find other elders, including Bladeswift, Hammershout, Goldwell and Ironband. His response to a visitor paying homage to the olden races is warm and courteous.

Lunar Festival Emissaries serve as festival quest contacts in several regions. The Cenarion Circle’s celebration welcomes Azeroth’s inhabitants, and festival guidance directs visitors to a Lunar Festival Harbinger in the city, who can tell them more.

The Ironforge Reveler brings lively party enthusiasm to Lunar Festival chatter, praising Nighthaven’s festivities and the fireworks’ big booms. The reveler also talks about moonlight travel to Ironforge and warns that old faction grudges still matter back home, even while everyone is friendly at the celebration.

Deliana is a quest contact in Ironforge who bargains with adventurers for equipment and offers upgrades in return. Her own words show concern for her safety and impatience with the danger surrounding her work; she also speaks of Anthion and Bodley in connection with a medallion.

An Argent Dawn emissary who speaks for the order during the Scourge invasion. The emissary calls for Horde and Alliance forces to defend their lands and asks an experienced adventurer to investigate a suspected Scourge agent at Karazhan, then thanks them for the information they return.
An Argent Dawn paladin, identified with the Argent Dawn.
An Argent Dawn crusader, marked by the order’s name and the crusading rank it bears.
An Argent Dawn champion, carrying the order’s name and a rank that sets this figure apart from its crusaders.
A skeletal undead trooper whose combat routine includes Scourge Strike.

Lieutenant Nevell serves the Argent Dawn outside Ironforge, where the Scourge has appeared near the city. Nevell asks defenders to thin the undead ranks, bring proof of their defeat, and investigate strange glowing runic circles. After hearing the findings, Nevell suspects the circles carry voices used for communication, though the minds reached through them remain a troubling mystery. Nevell thanks the investigator on behalf of the Argent Dawn.
A Midsummer bonfire kindled at seasonal gathering places across Azeroth.

Midsummer Celebrants welcome visitors to the Fire Festival and point to its festivities, from dancing at the ribbon pole to torch juggling. Their words also carry a factional edge: Horde and Alliance celebrants speak of protecting their own fires and stealing the other's, giving the celebration a note of rivalry.

An Argent Dawn quartermaster, this representative directs those seeking orders against the Scourge to Light's Hope Chapel. Visitors can also ask to spend their runes, reflecting the quartermaster's role in the order's festival services.

The Festival Loremaster studies festivals past and documents the current celebration, while the Flame Wardens tend its fires. The Loremaster sees sacred flames as carrying power and suspects enemy cities guard such fires too. The stolen-city flames brought back by adventurers are recognized as coming from Orgrimmar and Thunder Bluff, and the Loremaster praises the daring involved in recovering them for the collection.
A herald of the Lich King who drives minions forward, boasts that their enemies' holdings will fall, and threatens to return with death and destruction when opposed.

Dwarf commoners celebrate Midsummer as a time for adventure, shopping and the closing fireworks. They regard the Lunar Festival as a special occasion to honor their ancient Earthen elders and consider their wisdom.

Gnome commoners enjoy Midsummer's celebrations, shopping and closing fireworks. During the Lunar Festival, they encourage seeking elders' wisdom and enthusiastically regard it as the best season to buy fireworks.
Max Xim is the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit arena battlemaster. He challenges would-be entrants on their ability and handles requests to fight in the arena battlegrounds.
Kandaar is the Eye of the Storm battlemaster, handling requests from those who want to join the battleground.

Farseer Javad trains shamans in the ways of the spirits and urges respect for the elements and their balance. He speaks warmly to a progressing student, expresses pride in their growth, and directs them to other farseers, including Nobundo and Eannu, for further instruction.
Keiran Donoghue is a sausage vendor who offers goods for sale.
The Barleybrew Apprentice sells Barleybrew and boasts that Azeroth has no better brew. Apprentices of this name serve as brew vendors in several regions.

Goldark Snipehunter is a Brewfest hunter nursing a knocked shin, so he recruits help to catch the elusive wolpertingers drawn by the festival. He supplies a net and offers Synthebrew Goggles for seeing them; his advice is that a proper hunt calls for being well-goggled.
